current_identity_checks: All five currently published source/protocol/cohort file hashes match SOURCE_FREEZE
Prior speaker1 pilot manifest SHA matches frozen dependency
Current cohort.protocol_sha and speaker roles match prospective protocol
Existing speaker1 pilot contains exactly the32 registered training members

findings.issue: Train/development acquisition does not itself validate SOURCE_FREEZE.files or cohort.protocol_sha256 against the current protocol. Current bytes match, but missing runtime fail-fast checks allow an unnoticed changed source/cohort to acquire data under a new receipt.
findings.resolution: Check every frozen source/protocol/cohort/helper hash and cohort.protocol_sha256 at the common acquisition/feature entry; preserve the existing published source snapshot if revised.

findings.issue: prefix(row) is a low-level unconditional decoder: confirmation authorization is only in acquire_role. An already-cached held MPEG could therefore be decoded by a caller that bypasses the acquisition entry.
findings.resolution: Require the same candidate/publication validation at the feature extraction entry before any held prefix call, or factor it into a common role guard used by both acquisition and prefix.

findings.issue: Raw cache reads in prefix are checked by length+CRC32, not by SHA256 from a frozen acquisition manifest. Actor1 prior SHA is checked only in the acquisition reuse branch; a newly acquired actor1 path also lacks that prior-SHA comparison.
findings.resolution: Bind every feature input to the role acquisition record SHA256 and source identity; use the known prior pilot SHA for speaker1 regardless of reuse/new-download branch.

review_kind: Read-only static/data-metadata audit; no new HTTP requests, MPEG byte reads, decoding or model execution
